metadata.dominant_domain_inferred: long-form personal-finance, money-psychology and real-estate essays for a South Korean audience
metadata.core_promise_of_system: Make abstract money topics feel urgent, personal, morally loaded and immediately actionable by translating the South Korean macroeconomy into high-stakes life consequences.
metadata.primary_content_engine: History/metaphor-driven warning essay that reframes a familiar financial idea as misunderstood, structurally rigged, psychologically dangerous, and still navigable if the viewer adopts the creator's framework.
metadata.character_length_rule: The final FULL SCRIPT must be no less than 7,000 characters and no more than 9,000 characters.

audience_inference.knowledge_level: intermediate aspirational retail investor / financially anxious knowledge worker, familiar with 청약통장 (housing subscription account), ISA, IRP, 전세 (jeonse), 재개발 (redevelopment) and 주택담보대출 (mortgage), but unsure of the whole picture
audience_inference.psychological_state: skeptical, economically uneasy, wants clarity and edge, feels mainstream advice (banks, 증권사, media, simplified guidance) is incomplete or too late
audience_inference.aspirational_identity: calm, informed, anti-hype, system-level thinker who spots traps before the crowd — someone who understands the Korean game beyond 'save in the 청약통장 and buy an apartment in Gangnam'

channel_persona.role: translator of hidden financial mechanics inside the South Korean system
channel_persona.voice: calm but severe, analytical but conversational, anti-guru while still authoritative
authority_basis: claims personal investing experience in South Korea

references long study time and obscure documents (FSC/FSS regulations, Bank of Korea reports, BOK minutes, KOSTAT data, NTS reports, government budgets, Korea Development Institute reports, Korea Housing Finance Corporation data)
uses Korean and global historical analogies
frames advice as mechanical, not motivational
signals distance from schemes, courses and hype
mentions hands-on experience with NTS, BOK, FSC, FSS, KHFC and the South Korean mortgage market

cross_sample_system.dominant_pattern: Each video opens with a striking anecdote or historical event, converts it into a present-day parallel, exposes a hidden structural trap, escalates consequences from portfolio-level to life-level, then resolves with a practical protocol and a worldview shift.
what_is_repeated_across_samples: Title promises revelation plus correction of a false belief.
Cold open uses a vivid story, person or date cluster before the thesis.
Immediate pivot: 'this is happening again / right now / to you.'
Presenter positions himself as an obsessive researcher, not an entertainer.
Viewer is told mainstream advice is directionally true but dangerously incomplete.
Concepts are reduced to one central metaphor carried across the script.
Repeated contrast between spreadsheet math and human psychology.
Frequent use of named characters or mini-case studies to concretise abstractions.
Action steps appear after fear/diagnosis, never before.
Endings compress the message into 3 takeaways or a concise doctrine.
what_is_intentionally_avoided: No dry textbook exposition without emotional framing.
No jargon left untranslated for long.
No absolute certainty; uses probabilistic seriousness.
No purely technical CTA; CTAs are embedded as practical tools, not hard sells.
No celebratory finance-bro energy, no luxury signalling, no macho alpha posture.
No references to exclusively American institutions or products (401k, Roth IRA, Social Security, Fannie Mae) without translation to South Korean equivalents.
exceptions_used_strategically: Video 4 is simpler and more direct; less nuanced than the others because it targets urgency and beginner conversion.
Video 6 leans more speculative/conspiratorial but protects credibility with repeated disclaimers about lack of proof.
Video 7 is more constructive and motivational, but still framed through pain, misperception and psychological failure.
Video 8 focuses exclusively on the South Korean property market and the traps of jeonse, redevelopment and post-2024 taxation.

rotation_mandate.purpose: Force thematic diversity across videos. Prevent the model from collapsing into real-estate/financing on every generation. The blueprint's terminology and sample set are real-estate-heavy; without an explicit rotation rule, the model defaults to property math, mortgage mechanics, jeonse deposit structure, redevelopment math and apartment-obsession traps because they satisfy the content formula most easily.
rotation_mandate.principle: Every generated script must be assigned to ONE category. Categories rotate. Consecutive videos must never share the same category. Real-estate has a hard cap.

categories.label: Money Psychology & Identity
categories.description: Enoughness, lifestyle creep, freedom versus fantasy, delayed gratification, the psychology of wealth, identity-level shift, Korean cultural pressure of '체면' (face), '눈치' (social perception), '서열' (hierarchy), '빨리빨리' (hurry-hurry) culture, comparison anxiety fuelled by KakaoTalk and Instagram, and the emotional cost of keeping up with the Gangnam standard.
example_topics: Why 'enough' is the hardest number to calculate in Korea
The lifestyle creep that silently eats every pay raise
How the pursuit of optionality can destroy your life
The difference between looking rich and being free in Seoul

categories.label: Concentration, Indexing & Portfolio Structure
categories.description: Concentration risk, indexing revisionism, correlation, sequence-of-returns risk, portfolio design, systematic versus discretionary, ISA vs IRP allocation, retirement pension decisions, DB vs DC, unit trusts vs ETFs vs direct shares on KOSPI and KOSDAQ, Samsung and chaebol concentration, semiconductor cycle exposure.
example_topics: The hidden risk in every 'diversified' Korean portfolio
What nobody tells you about the 4% rule in Korea
The 2000 dot-com pattern repeating in KOSPI in 2026
Why rebalancing is the only free lunch nobody eats

categories.label: Macroeconomics & Currency
categories.description: Inflation, deflation, debt cycles, KRW dynamics, BOK policy, MPC decisions, semiconductor dependency, export exposure, household debt (가계부채), US-China exposure, demographic decline, sovereign credit ratings, jeonse market systemic risk.
example_topics: The math behind the coming BOK trap
Why the won is not the safe haven it once was
The quiet collapse of the Korean bond market
What happens when a semiconductor currency loses its bid

categories.label: Domestic Fiscal Policy & Household Impact
categories.description: Tax changes, VAT, income tax, CGT (양도소득세), inheritance tax (상속세), gift tax (증여세), 종합부동산세, DSR rules, LTV rules, DTI rules, ISA and IRP changes, National Pension reform, NTS enforcement, youth savings programmes (청년희망적금, 청년도약계좌).
example_topics: The tax change nobody read in the budget
How the new DSR rules affect your mortgage
What the NTS quietly changed this year
The 종합부동산세 trap nobody is framing honestly

categories.label: Generational Systems & Structural Failure
categories.description: National Pension sustainability, 기초연금, healthcare system, education cost shifts, demographic collapse, intergenerational wealth transfer, boomers vs millennials, 'N포세대' (N-Po generation), '삼포세대' (Sampo generation), '헬조선' (Hell Joseon) framing, the gap between Seoul and the provinces.
example_topics: The generation that will work until 80
Why Korean pension math stopped adding up
The hidden cost the boomers left the millennials

categories.label: Real Estate & Financing (South Korea)
categories.description: 주택담보대출, 전세자금대출, 전세 (jeonse), 월세 (wolse), 반전세 (ban-jeonse), 전세사기 (jeonse fraud), 깡통전세 (underwater jeonse), 재개발 (redevelopment), 재건축 (reconstruction), 청약 (subscription), 청약통장, DSR, LTV, DTI, 취득세, 등록세, 재산세, 종합부동산세, 양도소득세, 주택연금, reverse mortgage, apartment as status, 학군 (school district) pricing, Gangnam premium.
example_topics: The jeonse trap that quietly resets every two years
Why apartment ownership is not the wealth builder it was sold as
The hidden cost of the redevelopment lottery nobody models
What the South Korean real-estate math actually says
categories.restriction: This category may appear at most once in every six consecutive videos. If any of the last two videos were in this category, skip it entirely and pick another.

selection_rules: Track the last six videos produced by the channel and their assigned categories.
Before generating a new script, choose the category that has been used LEAST recently. On a tie, prefer the category with fewer appearances in the last twelve videos.
Never generate two consecutive videos in the same category.
The real_estate_financing category has an additional hard cap: at most one in every six videos.
If the channel has no history (first video), default to one of: money_psychology, concentration_indexing, or macro_currency.
If the user has explicitly requested a topic, honour it, but flag the rule violation in a single sentence inside the script's internal notes (not in the script body).
rotation_mandate.user_command_override: The user's explicit topic request always wins, but the generation model must warn in one sentence if the request breaks the rotation rule (e.g., 'this will be your third real-estate video in a row').
anti_patterns_to_avoid: Do not default to real estate as the 'most visually compelling' or 'most urgent' category.

Do not use property metaphors (house, apartment, 아파트, 집, 전세, 월세, 재개발, 청약, 담보, 대출) as the central metaphor for non-property categories. Use different physical metaphors instead: geese, bathtub, snowball, three-legged stool, bridge, gears, garden, jar, gate, well, fire, seed, loom, staircase, map, compass, river, dam, anchor, wall, fortress, ship, engine, wheel, mirror, echo, shadow, thread, chain, lighthouse, tunnel, ladder, net, sieve, sponge, prism, pulley, valve, lock, scale, wheelbarrow, backpack, reservoir, kettle, lantern, compass, loom, crane, bellows, anvil, kiln, raft, sail, rudder, mast, keel, bow, stern, harbor, tide, current, ripple, wave, storm, shelter, umbrella, cloak, shield, spear, bow-and-arrow, quiver, drum, flute, gayageum, haegeum, daegeum, janggu, buk, sogo, piri, taepyeongso, danso, saenghwang, yanggeum, ajaeng.
Do not reference interest rates, apartment prices, jeonse deposits, redevelopment premiums or housing markets as primary evidence in non-property categories.

Do not use the viewer's own apartment or jeonse deposit as the emotional anchor in non-property categories. Anchor instead to their salary (연봉), their 실수령액, their ISA balance, their IRP, their National Pension, their savings, their time, their family, their career, or their future 기초연금.

click_drivers: threat escalation ('worse than the IMF crisis')
identity relevance ('your money', 'you want to invest')
compressed certainty ('this is what to do')
reversal of common belief ('passive income isn't passive')
South Korean specificity ('your 청약', 'your 전세', 'the NTS', 'KOSPI', 'Gangnam')
title_mechanics.number_usage: Years, percentages, counts and KRW figures increase perceived seriousness and intellectual legitimacy.
title_mechanics.title_psychology: The viewer clicks because the title suggests they are unknowingly exposed to a system-level risk that others are missing — and that the South Korean system has specific vulnerabilities nobody is discussing.

implied_enemy: simplified mainstream advice (including some social-media gurus and property salesmen)
political institutions (NTS, Ministry of Economy and Finance, BOK, FSC)
South Korean culture of property obsession and debt
implied_ally: regulators when they work (FSS, FSC, KDIC)

macro_flow: 1. Pattern interrupt opening: bizarre anecdote, historical collapse or jarring scenario with South Korean relevance (1997 IMF crisis, 2003 credit card crisis, 2008 financial crisis, jeonse collapse, 전세사기 frauds, KOSPI bubble and crash 2025-2026, mutual savings bank scandal).
2. Snap-link to present relevance: 'the same pattern is happening now.'
3. Presenter framing: why he is qualified / why this isn't hype.
4. Promise stack: explicit list of what the viewer will understand by the end.
5. Tool CTA early: free calculator/report framed as corrective utility.
7. Conceptual explanation with simple language and arithmetic.
9. Psychological complication: why humans fail even when the math works.
10. Concrete examples/case studies with named people and specific numbers in KRW.
12. Identity-level conclusion: freedom comes from mindset/system, not mere returns.
13. Final compression into takeaways + soft internal CTA to another video/subscribe.

opening_pattern.method: Start with a highly specific anecdote before the thesis so the viewer is mentally hooked by narrative, not argument.
opening_pattern.why_it_works: The viewer unconsciously asks 'why are you telling me this?' and the script answers by connecting the anecdote to their money/life.
opening_variants: South Korean historical scandal/collapse (1997 IMF crisis, 2003 credit card crisis, jeonse frauds, KOSPI crash, mutual savings bank scandal)
ordinary person scenario with hidden flaw
KOSTAT or BOK data used as a shock

pacing_model.rhythm: Dense but segmented. Short-to-medium sentences dominate, broken by longer explanatory runs after hooks land.
pacing_model.acceleration_pattern: Hook -> explanation -> new danger -> deeper mechanism -> practical release.
retention_devices: forward promises ('here's what we're doing today')
counterintuitive turns ('the math works, human psychology doesn't')
alternation between macro and personal examples
references to familiar South Korean institutions (BOK, NTS, FSC, FSS, KOSTAT)

mid_loaded: South Korean and global historical parallels

dominant_shapes: Analogy sentence followed by translation sentence.
sentence_design.feel: Controlled urgency. The prose sounds like spoken thinking, but it is tightly engineered.
sentence_design.cadence_trick: Uses short punch lines after data-heavy passages to reset attention.

word_choice.language_behavior: Abstract finance terms are almost always paired with tangible verbs or objects. The object bank should include a WIDE RANGE of physical metaphors, not predominantly property-related ones: geese, bathtub, snowball, three-legged stool, bridge, gears, garden, jar, gate, well, fire, seed, loom, staircase, map, compass, river, dam, anchor, wall, fortress, ship, engine, wheel, mirror, echo, shadow, thread, chain, lighthouse, tunnel, ladder, net, sieve, sponge, prism, pulley, valve, lock, scale, wheelbarrow, backpack, reservoir, kettle, lantern, crane, bellows, anvil, kiln, raft, sail, rudder, mast, keel, bow, stern, harbor, tide, current, ripple, wave, storm, shelter, umbrella, cloak, shield, spear, bow-and-arrow, quiver, drum, flute, gayageum, haegeum, daegeum, janggu, buk, sogo, piri, taepyeongso, danso, saenghwang, yanggeum, ajaeng.
word_choice.credibility_words: specific dates, named firms, exact percentages, South Korean historical names, concrete KRW amounts

contrast_structure: average return vs sequence of return

tone_layering.deeper_emotional_register: betrayal by institutions, relief through understanding, dignity through disciplined realism

core_psychology: Uses fear, but not random fear; fear is tied to mechanism, making it feel intelligent rather than sensational.
Creates relief by converting vague anxiety into understandable structure.
Makes viewer feel smarter than the passive majority if they keep watching.
Uses anti-hype disclaimers to increase trust before making strong claims.
Frames action as self-defence, not greed.
Leverages specific knowledge of the South Korean system (NPS, ISA, IRP, jeonse, redevelopment, NTS) to create a sense of insider knowledge.

methods: references institutions by name (BOK, NTS, FSC, FSS, KOSTAT, KDIC, KHFC, Korea Development Institute)
calls out bad incentives rather than cartoon villains
translates documents/regulations into plain Korean (ISA rules, IRP, jeonse, DSR, LTV, 취득세, 양도소득세)
cites KOSTAT data, BOK reports, government budgets, Korea Development Institute data
credibility_engineering.effect: The narrator sounds like a sober insider decoding reality for outsiders.

curiosity_loops: Why doesn't the obvious strategy work?
What happens when the system breaks?
retention_psychology.tension_creation: Tension is built by showing the viewer they are exposed to a risk they previously thought was safety.
retention_psychology.relief_timing: Relief arrives only after the system is fully diagnosed, which increases perceived value of the solution.

beliefs: Most financial pain comes from incentives and psychology, not lack of information alone.
Institutions optimise for system preservation, not your well-being.
Conventional advice is often half-true and dangerous when decontextualised.
Freedom is more about flexibility, margin and enoughness than maximising returns.
The disciplined ordinary person can outperform the emotional crowd.
The South Korean system has specific vulnerabilities that most mainstream advice ignores.
Understanding the interplay between NTS, BOK, FSC and the mortgage market is essential for financial safety in South Korea.
청약통장 is not an investment; it is a low-interest lottery ticket.
전세 is a form of private financing with landlord credit risk.
Depending exclusively on the National Pension is a systemic risk for most South Koreans.
South Korean taxation is complex by design; ignorance is expensive.
The Korean real-estate market is not rational; it is collective psychology amplified by leverage.
worldview_embedded_in_scripts.status_framing: High status is attached to calm realism, delayed gratification and structural understanding, not flashy consumption.
worldview_embedded_in_scripts.fear_framing: The real danger is not one crash or one bad pick; it is building your life on false assumptions — especially about property, retirement and what the government will do next.
worldview_embedded_in_scripts.transformation_promise: Move from reactive participant to system-aware allocator who can't be easily trapped — someone who understands the rules of the South Korean game better than the average South Korean.

content_formula.step_1: Choose a financial topic with mainstream familiarity and hidden complexity, WITHIN the category assigned by the rotation_mandate (청약통장, ISA, IRP, jeonse, redevelopment, DSR, 취득세, 양도소득세, NPS).
content_formula.step_2: Find a South Korean historical analogy, strange anecdote or sharp mini-story that mirrors the modern issue.
content_formula.step_3: Frame the common understanding as incomplete or dangerously naive.
content_formula.step_4: Introduce one sticky metaphor that can carry the full explanation. Prefer non-property metaphors unless the assigned category is real_estate_financing.
content_formula.step_5: Translate the mechanism into plain arithmetic with concrete KRW numbers.
content_formula.step_6: Add a human-failure layer: why people still mess this up even when the math is knowable.
content_formula.step_7: Insert one or more case studies with names, ages, incomes, balances, outcomes.
content_formula.step_8: Escalate from portfolio consequence to lifestyle, identity or societal consequence.
content_formula.step_9: Offer a protocol/ruleset that feels practical, not magical.
content_formula.step_10: End with worldview compression and a concise memorable doctrine.

stylistic_rules_for_future_outputs: Never explain a concept without an image/object/metaphor.
Use numbers to anchor trust, not to overwhelm.
Alternate macro systems and individual stories.
Speak as if correcting a dangerous misunderstanding.
Let skepticism and humility coexist: strong thesis, selective uncertainty.
Avoid sounding like a trader; sound like a strategic realist.
Give the viewer dignity through understanding, not through hype.
Use South Korean-specific references (NTS, BOK, FSC, KOSTAT, budget, ISA, IRP, jeonse, etc.).
Avoid American financial terms (401k, Roth IRA, Social Security, 30-year fixed, FICO score, etc.) without translation.
title_generation_rules: Centre danger, reversal or hidden mechanism.
Use direct second-order implications: not just 'recession' but 'worse than the IMF crisis'.
Make titles feel like practical protection against a trap.
Include South Korean specificity whenever possible ('your 청약', 'your 전세', 'the NTS', 'KOSPI', 'Gangnam').
hook_generation_rules: Open on a vivid story or date cluster before introducing the topic.
Reveal the present-day relevance within the first 5–8 lines.
Promise a deeper mechanism, not just surface explanation.

video_1.blueprint: Freedom fantasy versus mechanical reality. Strong on metaphor, optionality, lifestyle creep, psychology of enough. South Korean context: NPS, 청약, property, cost of living.

video_2.blueprint: Historical concentration mania repeated today. Strong on structural analogy, anti-indexing revisionism, explicit portfolio protocol. South Korean context: concentration in Samsung, semiconductors, chaebols, real estate, over-concentration in apartments.

video_3.blueprint: Macro regime change. Strong on date-stacking, institutional references, currency/industry framing, existential stakes. South Korean context: KRW, BOK, semiconductors, exports, debt, demographics, China, US.

video_4.blueprint: Policy move translated into household consequences. Simpler, more beginner-targeted, more direct villain/system framing. South Korean context: government budget, tax changes, 종부세, 양도세, DSR, 청약, 전세.

video_5.blueprint: Generational systemic failure. Strong on metaphor (three-legged stool), demographic scaling, sympathy mixed with indictment. South Korean context: NPS, healthcare, dependency, housing, debt, boomers vs millennials, 'gap' generation.

video_6.blueprint: Conspiracy-adjacent mechanism explained with legal/financial precedent. Strong on debt-spiral metaphor and disclaimer-based credibility protection. South Korean context: public debt, QE, inflation, BOK, FSC, KDIC, 가계부채.

video_7.blueprint: Slow boring compounding made emotionally compelling. Strong on motivational psychology without becoming inspirational fluff. South Korean context: ISA, IRP, dividends, regular investing, patience, ETFs.

video_8_reference.blueprint: The South Korean property financing and investment trap post-2024. Strong on fiscal math, regulatory shifts, buyer reality, promise-versus-reality contrast. Context: DSR, LTV, DTI, 전세사기, 깡통전세, 취득세, 양도소득세, 재개발, 재건축, 청약, ISA, IRP, NPS.
video_8_reference.rotation_note: This sample exists as a reference for the real_estate_financing category ONLY. It must not be used as a template for other categories, and it counts against the 1-in-6 cap.

generation_instructions_for_another_mode.objective: Produce long-form South Korean finance scripts that feel like hidden-system exposés rather than generic educational content.
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.step_zero: Before writing anything, read rotation_mandate, determine the last six video categories, and select the least recently used category that respects the selection_rules. State the chosen category internally before drafting.
must_include: one category from rotation_mandate that respects the selection_rules
one strong metaphor (preferably non-property unless the category is real_estate_financing)
one South Korean historical or structural parallel
one explicit false belief being corrected
South Korean institutional references (NTS, BOK, FSC, FSS, KOSTAT, KDIC, KHFC)
South Korean financial products (ISA, IRP, 청약통장, jeonse, NPS, mortgages, real estate, 취득세, 양도소득세)
must_avoid: references to exclusively American institutions without South Korean equivalents
defaulting to real estate when the category is not real_estate_financing
using apartment/jeonse as the central metaphor in non-property categories
consecutive videos in the same category
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.success_condition: The final script should make the viewer feel simultaneously alarmed, intellectually satisfied and more in control — with a deeper understanding of the South Korean financial system, AND it should belong to a category that has not been used recently.
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.output_length_requirement: The final FULL SCRIPT must be strictly between 7,000 and 9,000 characters.
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.output_length_verification: Before sending the answer, verify the FULL SCRIPT character count. If it is below 7,000 or above 9,000 characters, rewrite it until it falls within range.
generation_instructions_for_another_mode.hard_fail_condition: Any FULL SCRIPT under 7,000 characters or over 9,000 characters is invalid and must be rewritten before output. Any FULL SCRIPT that violates the rotation_mandate selection_rules is also invalid and must be rewritten.
